There's a difference between celiacs, gluten intolerance, and the "gluten intolerant" like this video is talking about.

Real celiacs will lose the ability to properly digest any food with very small doses. It will take a month for their intestines to repair the damage. Might be an intolerance. Allergy specialists sometimes call it a sensitivity if it's an intolerance that requires a extremely high dose or has low severity effects. Intolerances aren't quite the same as allergies, which tend to have a very low threshold for quantity (like reusing a cutting board). The confounding thing is that it's easy to test for allergies to things that are not food, but for things that ARE food, they turn into other stuff in your gut, bacteria does more things to it, and nobody is going to inject you with half-digested stuff.

I can butter my bread and eat most cheese, but if I drink a glass of milk or eat a bowl of ice cream, my next couple days (and those of everyone around me with noses) are ruined. That's an intolerance. I'm not going to eat cannoli or chowder, but otherwise I eat what I want. Worst I do is tell people to avoid following the "extra creamy" versions of a recipe. Size the island to your likings. I wouldn't make it too big, as it would ruin a bit of the challenge, but feel free to limit it to produce more of a challenge. Again, 'tis your choice.The chest materials should DEFINITLEY include : 2 block of ice, and a bucket of lava. It would also be ideal to include : 1 catcus block, 1 sugarcane, 1 of each mushroom, 1 bone, 1 melon seed, 1 pumpkin seed. That way you can easily obtain these otherwise unobtainable blocks and reproduce them. Some people also make additional [smaller] islands far away from the initial island that has other things, such as obsidian for venturing to the nether.
